title: Non-Equilibrium Phononic Phenomena on nm × ps Scale Revealed by Five-Dimensional Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) and scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) are the fundamental tools for the modern material and biological science due to its potential to visualize nanoscale structures. Although time resolution of conventional TEM and STEM is limited by the shutter speed of camera and scan speed of electron beam, recent advances on ultrafast electron microscopy technique that uses ultrashort electron pulse enables to observe ultrafast dynamics after photoexcitation on ultrafast (fs-ns) temporal scale. Ultrafast electron microscopy and diffraction have been utilized to reveal various structural and magnetic phenomena such as structural phase transition [1], acoustic wave propagation [2], and magnetic dynamics [3].
